_readme: Codex's item wire vocabulary, for the keys BOTH the Go provider and the TS renderer plugin spell. Codex streams a command's output as a run of `outputDelta` events and fills `aggregatedOutput` only on the COMPLETED item, so a turn that ends first leaves an item with no output at all. LeapMux joins the deltas and stores the join beside the frame; `supplement` lists the keys of that envelope and `item` lists the fields of the frame it joins onto. Both sides run the same resolve -- the worker for its semantic extractors, the browser for the row it draws -- so a drift between two hand copies puts a retained command row on screen with its output missing and nothing to say so. `collabItem` lists the two fields of a collab tool call that both sides read to list the subagents one launch created. OpenAI owns the `item` and `collabItem` field names; LeapMux owns the supplement keys. `options` and `optionDefaults` hold the four Codex option axes LeapMux surfaces -- the option-group id of each, and the value an agent starts at when the row stores none. The worker builds the option groups from them and applies the default at launch; the browser seeds a new agent with the collaboration mode and reads the same id for its plan mode and its trigger. A default that differed between the two started an agent at one value and drew another. LeapMux chose the option ids; OpenAI owns the values.

CodexToolSupplement.doc:
CodexToolSupplement is the output LeapMux joined for a tool call that reported
no completed item of its own.

Codex streams a command's output as a run of `outputDelta` events and puts the
whole text in `aggregatedOutput` only on the COMPLETED item. A turn that ends
first leaves the started item, which has no output at all, so the join is the
only copy. It identifies the item it belongs to, so a row cannot take another call's
output.
